data.title: Carvana Stock (CVNA) Falls 14% in a Month, But JPMorgan Rejects 'Muse-Mageddon' Fears — Here's Why
data.description: It's been 24 days since social media giant Meta (META) launched its Muse AI agent to widespread applause on Wall Street. Interestingly, shares in used-car retailer Carvana (CVNA) have fallen by about 14% over the past month to about $64. This comes amid fears that AI agents shopping for the cheapest deals on users' behalf could disrupt Carvana's business model. However, JPMorgan's four-star Rajat Gupta has pushed back against these "Muse-Mageddon" fears. He pointed to Carvana's competitive used-vehicle prices and auto loan rates, among other factors.
data.author: Solomon Oladipupo

data.title: Apple (AAPL) Launches New Safeguards Against AI Agents
data.description:
Apple (AAPL) is launching new safeguards to defend its electronic devices against probing artificial intelligence (AI) agents. The iPhone maker said that it plans to update its controls regarding "Full Disk Access" in its macOS operating system in response to AI agents potentially probing user data on its devices that also include the Apple Watch and iPad.

The Silicon Valley-based company warned that developers using "Full Disk Access" can expose everything on their systems to AI agents, including files, email, private messages and browsing history. This not only creates potential privacy issues for the user but also for other people that a user communicates with.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Meta Stock Gets $885 Target, but Muse Growth Raises Monetization Question
data.description:
Social media giant Meta Platforms (META) is getting more praise from Wall Street as its Muse AI agent continues to attract users. Muse has now topped 5.6 million downloads since its September launch and remains the No. 1 app on Apple's (AAPL) App Store. Five-star BNP analyst Nick Jones, who is ranked #223 out of 12,504 Wall Street analysts, kept a Buy rating and an $885 price target on Meta. However, he believes that the bigger question is whether Meta can turn that early interest into regular use and meaningful revenue.

Interestingly, Muse's strong start partly reflects Meta's massive distribution advantage. The company can promote the AI agent through Facebook and Instagram, which gives it access to billions of existing users. As a result, BNP said that Muse's early U.S. downloads surpassed both ChatGPT and OpenAI's Sora.

However, downloads do not necessarily translate into long-term engagement.

Promotion

METQ: built for a short position on META

Jones noted that Muse's open rate has stabilized below several established apps. This suggests that Meta still needs to give users reasons to return regularly even though they are interested enough to download it. That next step will also determine how much money Muse can eventually make.

Advertising Could Become Muse's Bigger Opportunity

Muse is currently free at the basic level, while higher usage requires a subscription. Meta also takes a small fee from some transactions completed through the agent. Nevertheless, Jones believes that advertising could eventually become another major revenue source if engagement rises.

That would actually fit Meta's existing business model, where advertising already generates most of the company's revenue. Muse could also create new opportunities as Meta adds shopping and business tools. For example, the company recently expanded Muse integrations for small businesses, including Shopify (SHOP) and Stripe.

However, competition is starting to increase. OpenAI launched its Dots AI agents this week. The service initially focuses on professional users and can carry out tasks through apps such as Slack and Microsoft (MSFT) Teams. OpenAI plans to expand its agent strategy over time.

For now, BNP does not expect Muse to seriously threaten specialized online marketplaces because it still lacks their inventory and customer-service infrastructure.

What Is the Price Target for Meta?

Overall, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on META stock based on 40 Buys, six Holds, and zero Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average META price target of $800.90 per share implies 9.4% upside potential. (See META Stock Forecast).

data.title: Nike (NKE) Defends Its Dividend as Company Restructures
data.description:
Nike (NKE) is defending its dividend payment as its finance deteriorate and it undertakes a restructuring of its operations meant to cut costs and conserve cash. Currently, Nike pays a quarterly distribution to stockholders of $0.41 per share. That gives the slumping stock a yield of nearly 5%, one of the highest payouts among the 30 constituents in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

Some analysts have suggested that the sneaker giant could cut its dividend to help conserve cash and give the company money needed to help fund its ongoing turnaround strategy. However, management defended the dividend on their most recent earnings call with analysts and media, saying the distribution is safe for now.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: S&P 500 Top Stock Gainers Today, 10/2/26
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) ended the trading week on a high note, finishing Friday with a 0.74% gain. Falling interest rate expectations boosted by a weaker-than-expected jobs report helped support equities. Consumer discretionary led all sectors with a 1.38% return, while healthcare stocks lagged with a 0.03% loss.

Let's break down the sectors behind the performance.

Today's Top-Performing Sector 

Consumer discretionary was the top-performing sector, with Tesla (TSLA) leading the group higher after announcing 486,532 deliveries in the third quarter, topping expectations of 461,000. Cruise stocks also rallied following an earnings beat from Carnival (CCL), with Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH) and Royal Caribbean Cruises (RCL) trading higher in sympathy.

data.title: Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Slides as Paramount Keeps Major DC Components
data.description:
Entertainment giant Paramount Skydance (PSKY)—soon to be just "Skydance"—had its share of outstanding questions going forward from the merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). That merger has not happened yet, but should be finished in the next few days. One of those outstanding questions focused on the DC Studios operation, and has now been resolved. This good news was not good enough for investors, though, as shares slipped modestly in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Paramount has seen a 51.07% loss in its share price over the past year.

Still In and Swinging

The big question for Paramount and DC Studios came down to whether or not they would get rid of James Gunn and Peter Safran, the current heads of DC Studios. And even as Paramount is cleaning house, this was a part it decided not to touch, leaving both Gunn and Safran in to run the combination film, television, and comic book operation, according to a report from Deadline.

Gunn has already been hard at work getting Clayface ready for its October 23 release, and the Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow, ready for July 9, 2027. Given that Superman was Warner's second-highest-grossing film at over $618 million, there is every reason to let Gunn cook. And it seems like Paramount seems inclined to do exactly that.

There is the Star Trek series, of course, which has seen better days, but still represents a long-term money-maker with piles of name recognition. It has every property from Adult Swim to work with, the entirety of DC Studios—as mentioned previously—everything in the Discovery Family Channel, Nickelodeon, and plenty more besides. It will also have New Line Cinema, which means that it will likely have two Nightmare on Elm Street titles coming out soon.

data.title: GameStop (GME) CEO Ryan Cohen Buys $10 Million of Company Stock
data.description:
GameStop (GME) CEO Ryan Cohen continues to load up on shares of the company he runs. Regulatory filings show that Cohen bought 450,000 shares of GME stock for $10.6 million on Sept. 29, bringing his direct holdings to just over 40.9 million shares, a stake worth $998.36 million or 8% of the video game retailer.

The purchase on Sept. 29 was Cohen's third major buy of GME stock in less than a month. The CEO acquired $20.4 million worth of shares on Sept. 10 and an additional $26.3 million of company stock on Sept. 21. Other members of senior management have also been buying GameStop's stock. On Oct. 1, Nat Turner, who sits on the company's board of directors, bought 10,462 shares for $24.33 apiece, bringing his purchase to $252,238.

Alignment with Stockholders

Why Cohen has been loading up on GME stock isn't clear. However, earlier this year, he said that it is important for chief executive officer's of public companies to buy stock with their personal funds "in order to further strengthen alignment with stockholders." Many other CEOs purchase company stock for the same reasons, including Greg Abel, the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B).

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Sinks as it Keeps Number 3 Sales Position in the Third Quarter
data.description:
Good news, of a sort, arrived for legacy automaker Ford (F). A report from CNBC noted that Ford managed to hold on to its position as the third-largest seller of vehicles in the United States. This turned out to be much closer than expected, as Ford nearly dropped to number four behind Hyundai Motor (HYMLF). That near-miss cost Ford, though, as investors dealt Ford shares a fractional loss in Friday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 3.16% loss in its share price over the past year.

Pronounced Sales Drop

Ford reported that it turned in a sales decline of 6.6% for the third quarter, posting a grand total of 507,395 light-duty vehicles sold. This does not include heavy-duty vehicle sales, the report noted, as those are considered under different figures. But this figure, as disappointing as it might have been, still managed to succeed against Hyundai, who posted 506,200 vehicles sold in the quarter. This was up 5.4% against the previous year's third quarter, the report noted.

Last week, Cox Automotive posted a forecast that said Hyundai would outsell Ford this quarter, which would have been the first time such a thing had happened. But thanks to that narrow win, Ford managed to hold its position in the top three of sales. Ford, for its part, noted that this has been an unusual year, as it faced several out-of-the-ordinary supply chain issues and discontinued some of its biggest sellers, like the Ford Escape. This point is not lost on those who said that it was a bad idea to stop selling the Escape to begin with.

A Solar Win

Meanwhile, Ford picked up a bit of a win for green technology, as it will tap into a new installation recently finished in Coldwater, Michigan. The 100-megawatt Cold Creek Solar Park was recently put in place by DTE Energy (DTE), and the power that park generates will in part go into Ford's operations. Ford, for its part, agreed to buy as much as 650 MW of renewable energy from DTE via the CleanVision MIGreenPower program.

Ford still plans to make every Ford vehicle assembled in Michigan assembled with "…the equivalent of carbon-free electricity…" before 2027 ends, noted a report from Solar Power World.
